title: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 12 Red Dragon, Red Herring

sense.text: This is a continuation of the Book of Revelation; the captains should know how to break down Revelation 12. John the Revelator was in a prison camp on the island of Patmos, a salt mine, writing around the year 96 AD; Jerusalem had already been destroyed. About 85% of the Book of Revelation is written in parable form, metaphor and allegory, and to understand it you must know the Old Testament precepts. “A woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet”: this woman is not so much Mary; it goes beyond Mary, and her name wasn’t Mary, which is Greek; her name was Miriam. The woman represents the nation of Israel, and she is clothed with the sun and the moon because they represent God’s law. “And upon her head a crown of twelve stars”: the twelve stars represent the twelve tribes of Israel, so this woman is the nation of the twelve tribes.

precepts.why: “I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman”: the Lord considers us a beautiful and delicate woman. That is the woman Revelation 12 is talking about.
“And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night”: the word to see is lights. The sun is the greater light; the moon is the lesser light.
“For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light”: so now we understand why Israel was clothed with the sun and the moon was under her feet. It represents God’s law.

This is Joseph: “Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me.” His father asked, “Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth?” This was the formation of the twelve tribes of Israel; each son was represented as a star. So when Revelation 12 says “upon her head a crown of twelve stars,” it is the twelve tribes.

sense.text: “And she being with child cried, travailing in birth, and pained to be delivered”: why were we crying? Because we were in captivity under Rome. We cried to be delivered; we were waiting for the Saviour. The angel told Mary what to call the son, because he was going to save his people from captivity, and we are in captivity because of our sins. That relates to us today: where are we today? In captivity, and we are pained to be delivered.

precepts.why: When we explain Matthew the first chapter we generally go to verse 21, but many times we omit a main part. “And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary”: here Matthew gives Joseph’s genealogy. “From David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations”: as teachers, pause at Babylon, because Babylon were our slave masters. “And from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations”: after the Babylonian captivity came the Medo-Persian captivity, then the Greek captivity, then the Roman captivity, wherein Christ was born. “Before they came together” means before the wedding feast, and Joseph was “minded to put her away privily,” because it was a shame for a woman to be pregnant before the wedding feast. It was never all right for a woman to be pregnant without being married. “For he shall save his people from their sins”: why do we need to be saved? Because we were in captivity, slavery. This is what the average black Christian doesn’t understand; they read this and forget all the captivities recorded in verse 17. As teachers, emphasize verse 17 and jump down to verse 21: this is why we needed saving.

A side note for teachers: Luke gives Mary’s genealogy. “The son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli”: Matthew says Joseph was the son of Jacob, so this Heli is on Mary’s side. Heli was Mary’s father, so Joseph was the son-in-law of Heli.

sense.text: “And behold a great red dragon”: the color stipulation is Esau, red, and dragons make reference to mankind, so the great red dragon is Esau, the children of Edom. “Having seven heads”: the seven major empires, Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Britain. “And ten horns”: the ten common markets, also called the EU: Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Denmark, Ireland, England and Greece. Write it in your Bibles. “And seven crowns upon his heads”: because these were world empires.

precepts.why: Genesis means beginnings; this is the origin of two nations. “Two nations are in thy womb.” “And the one people shall be stronger than the other people”: that’s us. “And the elder shall serve the younger”: that is prophetic for the kingdom. “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau”: that is the first time in the Bible red was used in terms of complexion for a human being. Before that everybody looked like Adam, from the dust of the ground.
“I am a brother to dragons”: this is what Job said, so dragons make reference to man too. Put the color red together with the dragon, mankind, and the man this dragon is making reference to is Esau.

sense.text: “And his tail drew the third part of the stars of heaven”: remember there were twelve stars; divide them up and the third part is four. That is Judah, Benjamin, Levi, and remnants of the northern kingdom that were amongst us. That is why in John 4 you read about the Samaritan woman, which was of Ephraim, and in Luke about Anna of the tribe of Asher. “And did cast them to the earth”: into captivity. The great red dragon is Esau, Idumea, the Roman Empire, and God is calling them the devil: jump to verse 9, “And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil.” We are not saying it out of any personal hatred; it is strictly biblical, and this is what the scholars have been hiding from us for centuries.

precepts.why: This explains the dragon, the woman and the child. “Take the young child and his mother”: the young child is Christ and his mother is Mary. “For Herod will seek the young child to destroy him”: the Bible dictionary says Herod was an Idumean ruler, and Idumea is the Greek and Roman name for Edom. That’s Esau. That is why we went to Genesis 25 to explain the red dragon was Esau, and here is further verification. “And the dragon stood before the woman which was ready to be delivered, for to devour her child as soon as it was born.”

sense.text: “And she brought forth a man child”: that’s Christ, “who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron.” “And her child was caught up unto God, and to his throne.”

precepts.why: “He was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.” “Why stand ye gazing up into heaven?” They stood there gazing because they had never seen a man fly like that; they were looking at the Son of God ascend into heaven into a chariot. “This same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.”

sense.text: “And the woman fled into the wilderness”: this still goes with Matthew 2:13, where the angel said flee into Egypt, deeper into the land of Ham. The wilderness is Africa. You could walk from Israel into Egypt until they built the Suez Canal and cut it off, and from Egypt you can get through the Sudan down to Ethiopia, or towards Libya and Algeria, down to Niger, Chad and Mali. Find out where they got the slaves from, because the slaves fit Deuteronomy 28; they did not just get them from Ghana. We did a class about slaves taken from Mozambique. “Where she hath a place prepared of God”: that place is America. “That they should feed her there a thousand two hundred and threescore days”: write this down. 1,260 divided by 360 days, because that is how many days the years were back in the day, not 365, equals three and a half, which is 350 years. That is how long we are going to be nourished here.

precepts.why: For those who say how do you know they went further into Africa. “From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia my suppliants, even the daughter of my dispersed”: when we fled into Africa we fled along those rivers, the Blue Nile and the White Nile through Ethiopia, Sudan, Uganda, Tanzania, down towards Mozambique, and we went further, towards Niger, Chad, Nigeria, Mali and Guinea. “I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people”: you really see that in Africa; not everybody is poor, but a large majority are afflicted and poor. “And they shall trust in the name of the Lord”: they have to be taught, and that is our mission. “The remnant of Israel”: it is naming who they are.

This is talking about when we left out of Egypt, but the precept shows what we did when we went deeper into Africa: “But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works.” Some of us set up our own empires and some of us joined. That is where the voodoo comes from, mingling amongst the tribes over there, and the language we adopted. Some say some of the slaves were Muslims; that argument is null and void when you compare it to the writings of the Bible.

This is for those who say Israel is not on the other side of the world. “Behold, I will save my people from the east country”: the east country is Africa. “And from the west country”: the west country is America, the Western Hemisphere, North, Central and South America. God is giving us a map of where his people have been scattered in slavery.

What is the place prepared of God? “In the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God”: this place is America. The teaching started here in the United States of America, not in Africa, the UK or the Caribbean islands.

sense.text: “And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon”: Christian commentaries will tell you there is going to be an angelic battle in the sky, with Lucifer coming out of the ground to fight. That is not what it is talking about. When it says Michael it means Michael, one of the four archangels; it is not really Christ. This is Esau’s seven empires and all their allies fighting against Christ and his angels.
“And prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven”: no more rulership for them upon the earth; that is what heaven makes reference to here.

“And the great dragon was cast out”: Esau is going to be cast out. “That old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world”: when we call them the devil and Satan it is not based on some personal interaction, and it is no prejudice thing. It is because the Bible says this.

precepts.why: “And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation”: what the world calls World War III, and the Bible calls Armageddon.

We already cleared up that the dragon is Esau; now we prove it. “That man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven”: this is talking about Christ. “To subdue the man that came out of the sea”: not the Atlantic Ocean; God divided the waters above the firmament from the waters under it, and the waters above the firmament we call space. That is the sea the man came from. “But only I saw that he sent out of his mouth as it had been a blast of fire, and out of his lips a flaming breath.”

Ezra asked the angel to break the vision down. “Behold, the days come, when the most High will begin to deliver them that are upon the earth.” “And one shall undertake to fight against another, one city against another”: when Christ returns it is going to be nations fighting nations, and he is going to interrupt that. “And then shall my Son be declared”: that’s the proof right there it is Christ. “Every man shall in their own land leave the battle they have one against another.” “And Sion shall come, and shall be shewed to all men, being prepared and builded”: that is talking about Israel. Now we have a more descriptive understanding of Revelation 12:7-9.

sense.text: “Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ”: after Esau goes down, the kingdom is the Lord’s. So anybody who thinks this kingdom ruling is Ishmael, the Arabs, is stupid. “For the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night”: this great red dragon is also called the accuser. Spiritually you can go to Job 1 and talk about Satan going before the Lord, but it goes beyond that, because Esau does the same thing. Every time you cut on the news they are accusing us of being the top murderers, the major evil in the earth, like Esau is so innocent. They accuse us day and night of not being the people of God, like Hosea 1:10, ‘ye are not my people,’ while they make movies about saving the Jewish people, God’s people.

precepts.why: “And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s”: after Esau goes down, the kingdom shall be the Lord’s. That is what we just read in Revelation 12; this is saying the same thing as 2 Esdras 6:9.

sense.text: That’s a heavy precept. We can’t overcome on our own. “And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb”: they overcame this great red dragon by the sacrifice of Christ. “And by the word of their testimony”: the testimony God teaches us about his son. “And they loved not their lives unto the death”: this group will put the truth of God before their own lives.

precepts.why: The Apostle Paul said there is always an internal battle between righteousness and unrighteousness, between good and evil within. “For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh: and these are contrary the one to the other”: you want to do the righteousness of God with your mind, but the flesh always wants to be pleased. It is a constant struggle.

What is the word of their testimony? “Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne”: the fruit of David’s body is Christ, who came from the loins of David. “If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony that I shall teach them”: we are only going to overcome with God’s testimony that he teaches us about his son. “Their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore”: talking about the kingdom of heaven.

Everybody has a personal testimony, but our testimonies are garbage, and this is why. “For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator”: for your testimony to be solidified you must die; this is why the New Testament stands firm. “Otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth”: while you are alive you could become a Muslim tomorrow; you could change your mind. The ones who left out of this truth all had testimonies, and they changed their doctrines. When a man turns from his righteous way, the Most High will not remember his righteousness. Your testimony is of no force while you’re alive.

sense.text: This is very heavy. “Woe to the inhabiters of the earth and of the sea! for the devil is come down unto you, having great wrath”: talking about this great red dragon. “Because he knoweth that he hath but a short time”: how does he know? He has scholars. YouTube, Facebook and Instagram are measuring platforms for this truth. Esau knows this truth has been going out; they are examining our understanding, our faithfulness and our zeal to determine where they are at time-wise. That is why they say we got to get them off YouTube; many converts are coming in through that platform. They monitor black people, but first and foremost they monitor this truth. They have this Bible in all their courthouses, and every president has a spiritual advisor to tell him where they are at prophetically. Esau is the devil, but he knows this Bible is true.

“He persecuted the woman which brought forth the man child”: after Christ died and was resurrected, that is when Rome really got down on us. As time grows shorter and shorter, this great red dragon will persecute the Israelites.

precepts.why: A side note: Esau’s kingdom stands because they all agree, Democrat and Republican playing good cop and bad cop. You may say liberals do many things for black people. “The vile person shall be no more called liberal”: notice what the Bible calls liberals, vile. A liberal sets up the United Negro College Fund; it may seem good on the surface, but it is meant to keep us docile and under the influence of negroism, so we never wake up to who we are. “To practise hypocrisy”: they say I’m against the Republicans, I’m against the conservatives, and the Bible says they are hypocrites, all working collectively. “He deviseth wicked devices to destroy the poor”: like welfare, a device to destroy the poor and divide the family: black woman, we’ll give you public assistance, housing, food stamps, just get rid of your man. There’s a plot behind everything they do.

sense.text: Verse 14 repeats verse 6 with more detail. “And to the woman were given two wings of a great eagle”: who was chasing the Israelites that made us flee? Rome, and their symbol was the eagle. “That she might fly into the wilderness”: deeper into Africa. “Into her place”: America; that is why we went to Hosea 1:10. “Where she is nourished”: the same thing as “that they should feed her there” in verse 6. “For a time, and times, and half a time”: a time is one, times is two, and half a time; three and a half, the same as 1,260 days divided by 360, 350 years. “From the face of the serpent”: the serpent is the one from verse 9, “that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan.” So the devil, Satan, our enemies, the white man is nourishing us here in America for 350 years.

precepts.why: “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth”: the symbol of Rome was the eagle. “A nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand”: they spoke Latin. “Until thou be destroyed”: they colonized us. “And he shall besiege thee in all thy gates”: Rome besieged Jerusalem, and we were under Roman persecution for seven years.

Compare Deuteronomy 28:49-53 with this. “And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies”: the Roman armies. “Then let them which are in Judea flee to the mountains”: the mountains of Africa. The Revelation said the woman fled into the wilderness, and the angel told Joseph to take Mary and Christ to Egypt; it gives you the direction. “And let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto”: you Israelites outside the country, don’t come back. “For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled”: what we just read in Deuteronomy 28; we had to fall into cannibalism and eat the flesh of our children because there was no food. That is why it says “woe unto them that are with child.” “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the Israelites that stayed back to fight, like the Zealots. “And shall be led away captive into all nations”: those that didn’t run and didn’t get killed. “And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles”: Rome, the white man, shall take over the land, until the times of the Gentile rule be fulfilled.

A side note; this came up in Uganda, when a Christian challenged us. “Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law”: the curse is Deuteronomy 28:15 down. The brother asked, if Christ redeemed us from the curse, why are we still oppressed? Go back to Luke 21:22: “that all things which are written may be fulfilled.” Christ came not to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfil, so everything Moses prophesied must happen to the children of Israel. Yes, he redeemed us from the curse, but there is a time period; everything must come to pass. The slave ship just happened, and now you can see the curses starting to be lifted off of us.

Here is the evidence prophetically that we shall be fed here: everything we have gotten here, the white man has given it to us. “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger”: food; “and in thirst”: water; “and in nakedness”: clothing; “and in want of all things”: education, religion, medicine, whatever you want. Moses used the word enemies; Christ used another term to John, the serpent.

sense.text: “And the serpent cast out of his mouth water as a flood after the woman”: his mouth is his media, and the water is deceit. That is why they got rid of Bill Cosby, who wanted to purchase NBC, and why they got rid of Bob Johnson, who owned BET, and the black news broadcast under it. The people who decide what you see are the executive producers in film and news and the editors-in-chief of the magazines. The media is telling you how to think, what to eat, what to wear, when to go to sleep; they decide to put the violin music behind a black child with flies in his eyes so you send all your money over there. Misinformation is a weapon of mass destruction. A red herring is something that misleads or distracts from a relevant or important question; it leads you to a false conclusion. After 9/11 they said Iraq had weapons of mass destruction, and after they destroyed Saddam Hussein they said they found none; it was a red herring, a ruse to get the oil. Here is Esau’s red herring today: the Jersey City shooting at a kosher market, and the articles on what are Black Hebrew Israelites. They always throw in black, so you’re not the real ones. The term anti-Semitic is a trigger word: there are at least seven Semitic families in the Bible. From Shem came Abraham and Isaac, and from Isaac came Esau, the white people, and Jacob, which includes blacks, Native American Indians and so-called Latinos; the Arabs are Semitic too. The articles said the shooters ‘expressed interest’ in the movement, but showed no evidence of it, and the attorney general said they had not established any formal links. They view white people as agents of Satan? That is what the Bible says; they would have to burn all the Bibles in the world for us not to have that view. They believe Jews are liars? Revelation 2:9 and 3:9 say that. Israel United in Christ condemns the attacks; the Bible says thou shalt not kill, and if we ever find any crazy brothers shooting guns or threatening to stab people, they got to go immediately. While all this is in the news, President Trump signed an executive order to treat discrimination against Jews as a violation of Title VI of the Civil Rights Act, interpreting Judaism as a nationality and not just a religion, so colleges risk losing their funding. While everyone is focusing on the imaginary Black Hebrew Israelite, he is establishing Judaism as a nationality through executive orders. That is a red herring.

precepts.why: “That he might cause her to be carried away of the flood.” “And carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive”: the sleight of men is their media, what we see on TV; that is the white man’s media.

When I read it I’m not stressed about it. Our president can write all the executive orders establishing Judaism as a nationality he wants, because here is the prophecy: “Also the robbers of thy people”: those who stole our land and identity, “shall exalt themselves”: as the Jews, the chosen people, “to establish the vision”: that they are the chosen people. Now you have executive orders to further establish the vision. “But they shall fall”: every last one of them. I ain’t scared, and neither should you be.

sense.text: “And the earth helped the woman”: the earth is the Bible, and the Bible is helping us, the woman with twelve stars on her head. “And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed up the flood which the dragon cast out of his mouth”: the Bible swallows every lie that comes out of the mouth, the media, of the dragon, lie after lie after lie, and they can’t take it.

precepts.why: “Truth shall spring out of the earth”: this Bible is going to be taught throughout the earth. The Bible is the earth that is helping the woman.

“And thine enemies shall be found liars unto thee”: everything the media puts out is a lie. “And thou shalt tread upon their high places”: that is when we get that power. We can’t do nothing now; all we can do is be at peace with everybody, read the scriptures and apply the scriptures. That’s our power.

When white people shoot up synagogues or schools they say the shooter suffered from some mental disorder, but they never say that about our people. Here is what the Bible says about our people: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart”: mental disorders. Gil Noble mentioned the post-traumatic slave syndrome, from the teachings of Dr. Joy DeGruy; we have never received any rehabilitation for the atrocities we have gone through since slavery. That word heart translates to mind; a large portion of us, not all, are mentally unstable.

sense.text: “And the dragon was wroth with the woman”: with the Israelites. “And went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ”: we are going to see more alleged things happening, like those two shooters, and they are going to blame the Israelites, blame the kidnappings on the Israelites. That is why, when things occur in the body through our congregations, especially if it is a detriment to any brother or sister, we must respond quickly and speedily. The media is waiting for one of us, and there are crazy men and women among us determined on bringing us down from within. We are in the midst of prophecy right now. Why is the dragon so wroth? Remember he knows he has a short time: they are watching Israel rise, and the women getting in order with the Bible, and that is one of the most difficult things on the planet. When people say you’re a Christian, that don’t insult me; the word Christian simply means anointed, and we are the true Christians, every man and woman in here.

precepts.why: We all have leisure time, but the media is waiting to take those images and videos to malign this truth. “Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed”: their goal is to blame the ministry. They are not going to say Tyrone did it; they are going to say an Israel United in Christ member did it. When an Edomite like Timothy McVeigh blew up the federal building, to this day it is hard to find out what church he went to. If you go to the gun range, that is fine as long as it is legal, but don’t put Israel United in Christ on it.

Next to this in your notes write red herring. “Hindered their building”: back then it was a physical building; today it is a spiritual building. “And by their secret plots”: these red herrings are popping up left and right, and they’re all secret plots, like the Lincoln Memorial video, where they tried to flip it on the brother who had nothing to do with it. “And popular persuasions”: their media; most people believe what they see on TV. “And commotions”: they try to stir up a commotion to get people against us. They were hindered from building for the space of two years, but they are not going to hinder this; it is going to keep going on until Christ returns.
Precepted with 1 Esdras 5: “Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house”: although 1 Esdras was talking about a physical building, now it is a spiritual building.

Step by step, here is how it is occurring. “The burden of Babylon”: the burden of America. “Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain”: the banner is the Bible, and Babylon is the highest mountain, the greatest nation on earth. In Uganda and Sierra Leone everybody wants to come to America, not realizing it is Mystery Babylon. “Exalt the voice unto them”: as we lift up the Bible. “Shake the hand”: rebuking, correcting the people. “That they may go into the gates of the nobles”: our people not wanting to be corrected go to the congressmen, the senators, the mayors, the governors and the president against the Israelites. They are told these people are not breaking laws, they have freedom of religion, so they come up with secret plots: send in informants, men and women, to bring them down from within, make them look violent, make them seem crazy.

This is Haman, an Edomite, speaking to the Persian rulers about the Israelites. “There was scattered a certain malicious people, that had laws contrary to all nations”: a different set of laws than all nations on earth. “And continually despised the commandments of kings”: they go against what man says. “Differing in the strange manner of their laws, and evil affected to our state”: now they are making laws that circumcision is barbaric; whatever we teach in the Bible, Esau is making laws to go against it. “Working all the mischief they can”: the mischief we work is teaching the Bible.

This is what Esau and the nations say, and wicked Israelites say the same thing: “Let us oppress the poor righteous man.” “Let our strength be the law of justice”: they frame mischief by laws. That is why Esau set up laws forbidding us to read and write, to perpetuate the lie that we are nothing more than Hamites and that Jesus Christ is a European. Now they are making laws against circumcision, and laws that your children must be vaccinated or get out of school, and then the parents go to jail; New York is going through that, and California already has the law. “He upbraideth us with our offending the law”: like John the Baptist told Herod it is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife. It is our job to tell all the nations to keep the commandments; Christ said whoever teaches men to break the least commandment shall be called the least. “He professeth to have the knowledge of God: and he calleth himself the child of the Lord”: that is who we are. “He is grievous unto us even to behold”: when they see the black image of Jesus in the Bible it grieves them. “We are esteemed of him as counterfeits”: when we say they are impostors, that is what the Bible calls them, counterfeits. Esau, you are not an Israelite; you are a counterfeit, an impostor, a convert. “And maketh his boast that God is his father.”

We close out here. “If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye”: if we are reproached for being in this truth we are supposed to rejoice. “But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer”: don’t say I’m being reproached for Christ when you’re in jail because you are a thief; the law says thou shalt not steal. If you are a pedophile, we are coming down on you with both feet; we are not going to support that. “Or as a busybody in other men’s matters”: don’t suffer for being nosy. “Yet if any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed”: don’t be ashamed for being reproached for being God’s anointed. “For the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God”: we are the house of God, so we expect tribulation to come. “And if the righteous scarcely be saved”: that goes with “they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony.” “Commit the keeping of their souls to him in well doing”: which means keeping the commandments.

Why will the righteous scarcely be saved? “For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”: it is a constant battle within our mind, to do righteousness or unrighteousness, to keep the law or break the law, to live a disciplined life or a carefree life, from when you wake up to when you go to sleep, even in your dreams. We’re in this fight, brothers and sisters.
